en: A huge block of ice drifted in from cold lands. In early spring it is a seasonal sight of sorts, but heaving it up with all your might and slamming it on a foe is an attack with no poetry whatsoever. Then again, the spray can make a rainbow afterward, which is elegant in its own way.

A sword with value as an antique. Overly ornate swords can rarely be counted on as weapons, and this one is no exception. Collectors prize its age and savor the character seeping from it, but it is a little unreliable to trust your life to.

Clerics say a spirit's attack seems to wound the flesh but really strikes the soul. Life is not whittled away because the body is struck; the body crumbles because life has been whittled away. Not that it makes any difference in the end.

Shockwave attacks are not so rare, but this wave is said to carry emotions along with the shock: the anger, fear or scorn the foe feels toward you. Tossed about by those feelings, your mind and body come apart, and you can no longer move, as if paralyzed.

A rod dark jesters use to reap their prey's lives amid mocking laughter. It is said to grow ever more vicious in answer to their cruel smiles. Its power calls forth more blood and carnage, and the mad revel only speeds up.

Heels whose points are sharp as spikes, with a toughness and power you'd never guess from their elegant look. One kick easily wrecks shoddy gear. A nasty weapon... but what if you were the one wearing them? Painful, dangerous, yet beautiful...! A rose without thorns would be dull, wouldn't it?

A robe worn by liches. It is highly resistant to Dark magic. Liches already belong to darkness, and on top of that they wear robes like this, so it is no exaggeration to call using Dark magic on a lich suicide.

en: Ask which fang truly has value to an adventurer, and one answer is a fang kept as proof of slaying a mighty foe. It can be a legendary beast's, or one from a foe you remember as "I could beat it easily now, but back then it took everything I had." It becomes a fang in the heart that spurs adventurers on.
note: Quoted phrase kept in quotes; wording compressed to fit 312. [editorial] quoted thought was ungrammatical

en: The claw of a stronger demon. Among the Kin of Darkness, front-line fighters likely all carry one. Even after its owner is slain, magic still lingers in the claw, and anyone weak of heart who touches it would be swallowed up in an instant.

A trident said to belong to the mermaid queen, symbol of rule over the sea. At sea, nothing can escape it. It calls whirlpools, gathers black clouds, and strikes down with lightning any who disrespect the sea. Fishermen greatly fear it for this.

A move that drives a clenched fist straight down. Simple, but the shock running from the crown down the spine is not to be taken lightly. Thrown with real hostility, it can even kill. This is no time to joke about it making you shorter.

A vine of the alraune, a bewitching flower. It looks thin, wiggly and flimsy, but it bends like a well-tanned whip and slices the skin. Even if you block it, it coils around you and pins you, so even veteran adventurers find it hard to fend off.
note: Alraune as in the item name 'Alraune Vine'.

en: The scale dust that cloaks a poison moth. It may spray the dust straight at you, or flit around scattering it. It also causes hallucinations, and many adventurers who scoff at a mere bug end up losing their lives.

Claw of a high-ranked dragon. A lesser dragon's intellect is little better than a beast's, but a greater one is a match for a human at least, sometimes wiser than us. If it wields its claw's power calmly and precisely, an average adventurer stands no chance.
A fan whose wings are finished razor-sharp. Thrown well, it reportedly can part a foe's head from its body, like the 'Takasago' play in the fan-tossing game tosenkyo.
note: Tosenkyo: Japanese fan-tossing game; 'Takasago' is one of its scoring patterns. 'Wings' = tsubasa (the fan's spread ribs).

en: A kyosoku is an armrest from a land far to the east. Lean an elbow on it in a relaxed pose and onlookers feel awed and cowed. A must-have for court nobles. So if such a person hurls their armrest at you, they are truly furious. Short of groveling on the floor, you won't be forgiven.
note: Tenjoubito = court nobles; dogeza = groveling on the floor.

en: A claw borne by beasts whose names are known across the land. They have evolved outside nature's laws, and the land will never make peace with them again. Yet that they survive anyway is proof of nothing but the power this claw holds.

Long ago, hearts grew desolate and the land was engulfed in war. When a king asked the dragons for help to end the strife, they gave him this Dragon Emperor Sword instead of their aid. Raise it high, and you can wield the dragons' power against the foe before you.
note: tasukeru kawari ni read as 'instead of helping directly'; king is 'him' (ou).

en: A strange art that calls brass-colored lightning down from the sky onto a foe at a thought. Unlike normal lightning, it does not pass through the body into the ground, but races around inside it until spent. Take a hit, and your body will be covered in worm-like burns.
Slime serves several purposes: keeping the body from drying out, helping it slide, catching prey, and so on. If you face a foe with slime, working out what it is for may lead you to victory.

A sword with an evil will. It takes over its wielder's mind and seeks ever greater power. So when it sees that a foe is stronger than its current wielder, it may even let the wielder be killed on purpose, so that the foe will pick it up.

Makes destructive waves by quivering. When a wave hits a body, it sets off resonance and destroys it from within. In theory, quivering in time with an incoming wave could amplify it and send it back, a 'wave return', but no one has pulled it off yet.

A big move: open wide and swallow the foe whole. Anyone would do it with a favorite food in front of them. Doing the eating is fine, but being gulped down to the stomach with a "Thanks for the meal!" is to be avoided at all costs.
note: itadakimasu / gochisousama joke: eating is fine, being eaten is not.

en: A halo is the glow behind a holy figure. We tend to embrace things linked to what we already embrace. The Demon Halo reflects the heart of whoever faces the demon. If that heart is steeped in evil, they will bow to its evil radiance, even though the foe is a demon.
note: hairou = halo (kouhai/gokou). Compressed to fit.

en: A hydra's fang. It is thicker and more firmly rooted than an ordinary snake's, so each bite really hurts. And since several heads are dealing them out, it stands to reason that hydras are strong.

A lamia's tail. Its supple muscles strike hard enough to knock a foe out in one blow. The tailed lower half is a snake's, yet it shares the human upper half's traits, so it's warm and lovely to touch or have coiled around you. Unable to forget the feel, people keep switching class to Summoner.
note: tenshoku = class change to Summoner (class name from corpus/HELP_TEXT). Compressed to fit.

en: The fly knights ever on guard around the Insector Lord, king of the flies. Besides their king, they also guard those the king approves of. Fiercely loyal and known to see every duty through, they are feared far and wide.
note: Insect Lord (insekutaa roodo) is a new name: the MONSTER1 name is not translated yet (slice_33); align when it is. [accuracy] Monster name as in MONSTER1 (review_g7): Insector Lord.

en: A sword that can fire spirits and dispel spirits. Hold it and you'll find it faintly cold, said to be because its guard is linked to the spirit world. Those who take it up, unless lifeless or free of any clinging to life, will reportedly have their souls seized by the sword.
note: Source typos: tsuba written with the 'spit' kanji (read as the sword guard); 'tamashii wo ken to torawareru' read as 'souls seized by the sword'.

en: A big move that acts on the air to form a pressure fault, then shifts it, catching the foe in the friction. The victim loses balance, gripped by a strange feeling, as if upper and lower body suddenly slid apart. Go along with it, and you'll be gently twisted, swaying, and torn apart.

A greatsword that embodies the Imperial Sword itself. Moving the Imperial Sword as if it were part of you is said to be the greatest trial for anyone who would bear the name Imperial Sword. So hard is it to handle that it's even said the sword chooses its wielder.
note: Source is self-referential (the name seems to be a title as well as the sword); kept literally.

en: The whip of the Hell Master, jailer of Hell. The common Hell Master is toned down in shape and power so adventurers can use it. So some adventurers are baffled by how the Hell Master's original Hell Master differs from their replica one. Of course, the genuine article is far stronger.
note: Name wordplay kept (monster and whip share the name Hell Master).

en: A fang of light that shines in rainbow colors. It is very beautiful, and depending on its clarity it can be worth more than diamonds and other gems. But each time it is used to strike a foe, its clarity drops, so very clear ones are extremely rare.
note: Source says 'attack with the claws'; generalized to 'used to strike'.

en: Fire too many Psi Blades -- that is, be attacked by all around for too long -- and in time the mind is transformed. However it is treated, it takes everything as an attack. It turns every emotion into hatred and grief and fires it out: that is Psi Blade +1. If a foe fired this at you, could you take it?
note: Source equates firing Psi Blades with a mind under constant attack (the '=' sign); rendered 'that is'. [editorial] the source's '=' gloss was hard to parse as commas

en: An arm blazing so fiercely it could fairly be called hellfire. A weapon borne by greater spirits and the like. You feel intense heat just standing near it, so friend or foe, take care when getting close to anyone with this arm.
Not the usual swallow-whole: an improved move that unhinges the jaw like a snake to swallow prey bigger than its own mouth whole. It's fine to watch an animal do it, but...
note: Trailing off kept. [proof] hyphenated noun 'swallow-whole' to match 2321

en: A claw as bright red as blood. That blood-like color is in fact a paralyzing poison. When it scratches, it pours poison into the wound and paralyzes the foe. Once the victim can't move, all that's left is to surrender to the claw's owner.

A whip that only chosen demons may wield. Netherworld hellfire spews from the grip, and each lash sends sparks dancing through the air. Struck by it, you'll not only be burned, but have your very soul scraped away.

A Great Wheel spinning even faster. There are many theories on the spin path that adds most power; some say an elliptical path with a fast-slow rhythm beats a near-circular one at constant speed. Why not master the Great Wheel yourself?
The scythe of Samael, a huge mantis-like skeleton that portends death. All who meet Samael are killed, so bringing its scythe home is considered a pipe dream.
note: Samael as in item name Samael's Scythe; 'its' used (gender unknown).

en: The deadly claw of beasts that have become legend. Its power is guaranteed: you will taste its destructive force, greater even than the rumors, with your own bodies.
A soul that wanders long as a wraith hones its grudge ever sharper. In time that grudge takes the form of claws, swung at the living.
A claw borne by the very highest class of dragons. Before it, ordinary armor and gear tear like paper. A legendary claw that it's said no one has ever brought back.

A saber borne by the dark knights. Strengthened by dark rites, it is tuned to bring out their full power. It can also petrify, so even blocking one blow is very dangerous. And if a high-ranking demon wields it, you had best be braced for the worst.

Claws of the very highest demons. Small as they look, they hide fearsome power within. Even a scratch could prove fatal. If you must face one, whoever first touches the other's body will be the victor.

What could be called the vessel of life for young homunculi. The flask has no special treatment, but it is reinforced by the will of the homunculi desperately guarding this home to survive. When that will breaks, their lives come to an end.
note: kanojotachi: homunculi referred to as female; 'their' keeps it plural without loss.

en: Armor painted in a picture, made real along with the monster inside it. It does have the defense its looks suggest, but no special abilities beyond that.

A legendary mad sword said to torment all who face it. Many adventurers have fallen before it. Now let us ask what adventure means. Even if you fall, you overcame fear and took the first step; a bright future as challengers awaits you. On your backs as you rise again, the moon smiles.
note: Compressed to fit 312; 'saichousensha' = challengers (trying again).

en: Headgear a grown homunculus wears to stay alive. It cannot yet live by breathing, so if this flask breaks, it will suffocate and die writhing. If you see a homunculus who broke its flask by accident, call an Alchemist for it before it is too late.
note: Homunculus as 'it' (gender not settled here). [accuracy] renkinjutsushi = Alchemist class (glossary), capitalized.

en: This dress gently intoxicates the heart like a sweet cocktail. A woman wrapped in it tints her surroundings a soft rose with her charm and the dress's.
Holy vestments that only the chosen among the nobles of the night may wear. Should an unworthy vampire put it on by mistake, it would crumble to ash at once.
note: Vampire as in chap corpus.

en: A robe imbued with the spirits' protection. Whoever wears it, that protection is granted equally. This likely stems from the fact that spirits, at root, are the land's system for circulating mana.

A cute headband made of roses. On fine days you can see alraunes making them together in high spirits. It invites sleep and confusion, so it's fine gear too. Filled with the alraunes' heartfelt care, these real roses never wither.
note: [editorial] 'fresh as they are' ambiguous (seiku de atte mo = even though real flowers)

en: Mail made for the Royal Honey by its worker bees. Its materials are a complete jumble, but the special defenses they give are not to be scoffed at. When it's damaged, worker bees come and patch it up, so it always looks brand new.
note: Royal Honey (roiyaru hanii) is a new name: MONSTER1 name not translated yet (slice_33). 'its' used, gender unknown.

en: A robe of humiliation sent to the defeated. No one wants to wear it, yet beaten knights nearly always don it by choice. Wearing it is a way to chasten their defeated selves and stay honest with themselves, and it carries the resolve to win next time and make the victor wear it.
note: [editorial] unclear subject 'It means'

en: A cloak adorned with rime from frozen lands. Any frozen tree will do, but lively green leaves frozen just as they were are thought best. Rime itself is rarely seen, so quality seems to vary wildly.
A breastplate for Evil alignment only. It is made for easy movement so as not to hinder its owner's attacks. Even if you aren't Evil, you'd want to try it on.

A silk robe that shines at midnight. It heightens the wearer's charm further, raising it to a beauty both graceful and alluring. Even if its wearer were one of the Kin of Darkness, you'd be entranced.

Nights when the sun does not set: such miraculous nights are called white nights. Cloth woven on a white night is said to hold the power of a sun that never sets. It offers some resistance to Priest spells.
A robe said to have been worn by the goddess who rules over serpents. Wear it, they say, and you can command every kind of snake. It also offers strong resistance to snake venom.
note: megami = goddess (source is explicit).

en: Armor worn by the "kings" among the Kin of Darkness who have a sovereign's makings. Lesser demons may not even know it exists, but greater demons would bow down at the mere sight of someone wearing it.

"Cheap" means shoddy or low-grade. This is armor scrapped as defective while making Iron Armor, which somehow reached the market. Armor guards your body, so every adventurer is willing to spend on it. The result: the worst armor of all, which won't sell no matter how cheap.
note: 'Iron Armor' is generic here (no ITEM.CSV row named aian aamaa found).

en: A shovel with uses to suit any job: digging holes, breaking rock, pounding wood. In battle it works as a spear and also as a shield. Normally it is just a tool, but in a farmer's or laborer's hands it makes a fine weapon. In a cook's hands, a fine frying pan.
note: Item name not yet in ITEM outputs (ctx shows the new-item marker).

en: A robe made for clowns. It looks extremely flashy, making a clown's every move seem even more exaggerated and fun.

A belly dress with the midriff and chest wide open. Spells raise barriers over the bare parts, so its defense is very high, and it strongly resists Holy and Dark magic. Bodily allure has long been an offering to the god of change. So do not ogle. If you can't help it, squint.
note: hengenshin = god of change (Ashtel's title per glossary); kept as the title, not the name.

en: A bucket made of tin. Surprisingly handy in all sorts of situations. Good for holding water, good for holding things, good for wearing on your head: it's at home anywhere. Truly all-purpose.

Inexperienced servants are not trusted with fine tea leaves. Being allowed to handle Greater Pekoe means nothing less than being recognized as a true servant. Fledgling servants watch their seniors handle these leaves and work hard, thinking, "Someday, me too."
note: Servant: lowercase, generic household servants (not the Servant class).

en: A planner packed with upcoming plans: a minute-by-minute schedule in meticulous writing. Things often don't go as scheduled, but fear not. It lists what to do in every foreseeable case at every point. Even what to do if you lose this planner is written in this planner.
A breastplate made of pearl oyster shell. The sea folk work the shell with a special process to make it. Perhaps that's why it has fair resistance to Mage spells.
This breastplate is presented to a clan's chief and is worked with more care than the usual oyster one. Its resistance to Mage spells is greater too, making it formidable armor.

Armor of the frenzied. While wearing it, you can turn madness into inner strength, making your physical abilities burst into bloom. The bizarre sight sends even allies fleeing. Attacking in such a state, you throw the foe into confusion as well.
note: Source typo kiteiteiru read as kiteiru.

en: A spear of light that makes even pure white light shine the color of darkness. Where it pierces, dark flames swirl up and burn the foe to nothing in an instant.

Claws of the demon kings. Even a fragment holds great power, so when giving a trusted subordinate a vital mission, a king may tear off a claw for protection. Attacked with these claws, with their boundless magic, or by one holding a weapon, you are in for a hard fight.

People praise freedom, yet cannot live without some lack of it. For those who crave obedience and servitude, this mace teaches what they must do and how they must live. Past a little endurance, they will taste the thrill of the gap between heart and body being filled.
note: Source keeps the innuendo; kept at the same strength.

en: A spear born of a demon god. Its destructive power is immense; one thrust is said to bore a hole in the earth. Forged with a grudge against the gods, it will show terrifying power if ever turned against a god.

Just an ordinary fallen tree. But being able to use it as a weapon means the foe has that much brute strength. Against a foe who can heft a fallen tree, you may want to think twice before attacking head-on.
A kitchen knife beloved in homes and kitchens. It lacks the edge of a legendary weapon, but its blade radiates the unshakable confidence of having cut through every ingredient there is.

A technique that flicks any object with finger strength, turning it into a bullet. Pebbles, beans, coins: anything will do. Mastering it is a real asset; there was even a Thief, "Pessel the Finger Shot", who aimed for the top with finger shots alone and got far, until an overcut nail forced retirement.
note: New name Pessel ([JP]); gender not stated, kept pronoun-free. [accuracy] touzoku = Thief class (glossary), capitalized.

en: A magic brush that can paint only what really happened. History is always written and handed down by the victors to suit themselves. But this brush lays everything bare in broad daylight, convenient or not. That is why the powerful once loathed it and ordered it destroyed, it seems.
note: Item name not used in the text (name not yet fixed).

en: A throwing knife carried by Jokers. A special treatment keeps it silent in flight. Thrown from the shadows, it can deal a fatal wound even to a veteran Fighter. And once the victim can no longer move, the Joker appears, grinning from ear to ear.
note: Joker = the monster (MONSTER2). [accuracy] senshi = Fighter class (glossary), as in review_g5.

en: Swing it down hard and fast to pound mochi that is smooth and springy. When pounding mochi, keeping time with the partner who turns the dough is vital. One slip, and that partner's hand is mashed to a pulp, and the mochi turns bright red.

A splendid leaf, beautiful and firm. Its fibers are tightly intertwined, so it cannot be cut easily. This Flower King's Leaf purifies the air extremely well, enough to always supply fresh air even with no other plants around.

A buckler carried by Abi. "Shield in the right hand! Shield in the left too, that's double! Raise them by the face, five times! Run, ten times! Total: a hundred times the defense!" So Abi cried when cornered, and charged to the front line.
note: Abi: gender unknown, no pronouns.

en: A shield carried by Abi. Abi's theory made little sense, and even if defense really rose a hundredfold, no fight is won by defending alone. Abi only realized this when the enemy copied the trick and gave chase.

A phantom fog spawned by Reckdas. It is said to spread so wide and thick it can blanket a whole town or land. Within this nightmare, fear is said to take real form; once frightened, even a great hero will soon be fleeing in panic.

The fist is interpreted in many ways; thunder is often called "the fist of the gods". Indeed, perhaps only the gods can bring down a parent's fist on humans and elves in this land. But if a fist of divine wrath truly fell, we could only run away like babies.
note: [JP] = a parent's scolding knuckle-punch; rendered 'fist' to match item name Fist +3. [editorial] 'Ideas of the fist' unclear

en: Some oozes are strongly acidic. Doused in one, armor melts and skin festers. Just how monsters keep such ooze inside their bodies is a fascinating question.

Light hitting a gem normally reflects and escapes as sparkle. But tweak that reflection with magic, and light can get in but not out. Give the light raging inside the gem one exit, and it will burst out as a single spear of light.
note: Compressed to fit 312.

en: The Progenitor: the vampire reigning at the top of the Kin of Night. Called the rulers of the night, they feed quite unlike lesser vampires. A single mouthful is said to sustain them for hundreds of years.
note: [JP] = 'kin of night' as in chap slice_021. [accuracy] Glossary term: Kin of Night.

en: It is said that, very rarely, someone bearing this factor is found in the land. How the factor arises, and what purpose it serves, are both unknown.

A huge, hard, bullet-like rock gouged into a strange shape. Its nature changes with its maker's will: it can harden further or explode on impact as needed. But scarier than any trick is the plain attack of giant rocks raining down like hail.

Claws painted jet-black. A set crest is carved into them, meant to amplify magic power. A simple scratch can do damage too. Where these claws scratch, the spot is said to throb with heat and swell up.

It freely wields long, supple tentacles, raining them down like countless whips. At the tips are things like a flower's pistils. They simply act as weights that add damage, but their true role is to suck out nutrients.
note: Subject (the monster) unstated in source; kept impersonal 'It'.

en: This shining pure-white liquid has a beauty that enthralls all who see it. It also smells sweet and tempts you to lick it, but licking the Milky Way means death. Yet it is said to be sweeter than anything in this world, so dying that way might be happiness.

Armor said to guard its wearer, its defense growing with the strength of the oath held in the heart. But should the heart waver or the oath be broken, the breastplate will lose its defense. For this reason, its wearers are sometimes viewed with respect.
note: Item name ([JP], not yet fixed) replaced by 'the breastplate'.

en: A claw turned white like marble. Whether from grooming or by nature is unknown, but it stands out among the claws of all races.
A bow possessed by the grudge of a beast of darkness. The grudge flies with each arrow; to the one shot, it looks like a savage beast flying at them, fangs bared.

A novice clown's outfit must look funny to make up for lacking skill. A seasoned clown, though, can create humor from within without relying on looks. So this outfit is tailored for ease of movement rather than a funny look.
note: [JP] = clown (wmap/chap).

en: A spear spoken of among the Kin of Darkness as a famed lance. It never breaks, and it is said that gripping it lets you feel the thoughts of its past owners.

The robe worn by the king of the netherworld. The whole robe is wrapped in darkness, and looking at it feels like being drawn into the dark. In fact, surrender to that feeling and your soul is said to be torn out and taken to the netherworld.
note: [JP] kept generic, not the glossary title 'Nether King' ([JP]).

en: A Water Shot uses ordinary water, but this Foul Water Shot is fired using filth: sewage, mud and the like. If you are hit, countless toxins and germs enter the wound; even if you win that fight, you will not live long, they say.
note: [JP] rendered 'Water Shot' to match Foul Water Shot (slice_17). [editorial] dangling modifier

en: A terminus bored into the world: that is a Nonsense Codon. As the world's end nears, they are said to arise in many places at once. Any event pierced by a Nonsense Codon has no future left. It can only begin its slow march toward death.

Slimy stuff feels awful stuck to your clothes or body. But if you give in, thinking "Oh, whatever," the discomfort turns dramatically into pleasure. Why not stop resisting and accept it just once? No responsibility taken if you can't come back from that world, though.
note: Compressed to fit 312.

en: Unlike an ordinary snowball, it is packed hard with magic, so it can withstand a fair amount of heat. If one is thrown at you, think less "hard snowball" and more "fist-sized rock".
Moisture in the air hardened into an arrow. Mages can produce similar ice arrows too, but snow spirits are said to fire five or six at once without even trying.

Water pushes back hard, so fish are surprisingly strong. This is their secret move: deftly using tail and fins, they knock a foe up, then smack the falling body sideways. Fishermen know its power well; with a green captain, you can watch the crew pop off the side of the boat one after another.
note: Compressed to fit 312. [editorial] 'Water resists hard' unclear; 'them' ambiguous (fishermen, not fish); direction: the fish knocks them off

en: A cruel move that crushes a foe under a huge foot. It looks like slow motion to an onlooker, but when targeted, your body freezes and you can't get away. And some stomps, even by feet of normal size, are said to inflict mental torment: fear and humiliation.

A costume for celebs, brought from a land far to the east. Many robes of different colors are layered so the colors show as stripes at the hem. But get carried away and pile on too many, and their weight will leave you unable to move, so beware.
note: [JP] (junihitoe); name not used in text.

en: A hooked-claw weapon made of bronze. Some are worn on the hand like gloves, but a monster's is usually part of its body. With the hardness of metal and a talon shape modeled on birds of prey, it can rip prey to shreds at will.

A heavy blow from a bronze foot. Rather than kick damage, it is built to "break" things through impact. The more precise and delicate the target, the greater the threat a Bronze Kick poses... Like, say, the human body.
note: Item name [JP] assumed 'Bronze Kick' (ITEM slice_18 not yet fixed).

en: A very sturdy, hard club. Get hit in the wrong spot and you'll pass out, no trouble at all.
A club studded here and there with nails and the like for extra killing power. Get hit and you'll be bloodied and off to heaven, nice and easy.

The student handbook issued at Santorea Academy. It holds a Mage's precepts in three scripts: Common, Ritual Magic and Spirit. Each year's classes teach students to read more, so each can learn the precepts suited to their power. The forebears clearly knew that neither too strict nor too lax will do.
note: Compressed to fit 312 (script names shortened). [accuracy] majutsushi = Mage class (glossary), capitalized.

en: A wind shock wave, so to speak. A Sonic Boom closely resembles the attack called Vacuum Blade. The difference is that a Sonic Boom damages the brain directly rather than causing wounds. An unseen attack on the brain is terrifying, and no amount of caution helps much.
note: [JP] = Vacuum Blade (slice_17).

en: A katana said to rival the legendary Murasame. Its blade evokes a tiger; whoever wields Kotetsu becomes fierce as a tiger and cuts down all in sight, they say. Its cut differs too: unlike Murasame, whose cut cannot even be seen, it leaves the wound in tatters.
note: New name Murasame ([JP]).

en: A simple yet razor-sharp sword. The blood of all it has cut has soaked into its blade, giving it a faint red glow. That blood grants its wielder the power of grudges. A dreadful sword that grows stronger the more people it cuts.

Said to be unleashed when a cursed spawn tears through its mother's womb to enter the world by its own will. A child born by nature's law, whatever its kind, is received and blessed by the land. But a life born without that blessing will have the land as its enemy from birth.
note: [JP] = 'cursed spawn'.

en: The blue flame rising from the ornate stand burns away the soul of all it touches. Unlike normal fire, it leaves not one burn on the body; it gnaws only at the mind. When touched by Blue Strike, what matters most is showing willpower that yields to nothing.
note: [JP] = 'ornate stand' (literal; context unclear).

en: A farm tool found anywhere. But in a Farmer's hands, it turns from tool to weapon. I once heard that farm tools evolved from weapons, and it seems that was right. Still, one would rather it were used properly.
note: Farmer = job (chap slice_010).

en: The ring around a sphere that always emits gravity is called a Gravity Ring; as the ring grows, so does the area of heavier gravity. But as it grows, the gravity waves disperse, so unless you get close to the sphere, it is not much of an attack.
note: Item name [JP] assumed 'Gravity Ring'.

en: A move where you leap at a foe and kick with both feet together. Botch the fall and the attacker is in danger too, but done right, its power is tremendous. The one kicked will likely drop whatever they were holding.
note: Dropkick (chap slice_002).

en: Wings that not only fly but also create shock waves when flapped. Their colors and looks vary: wings like a bird of prey's, bat wings evoking the Kin of Darkness, beautiful pure-white wings and more.

Form a sign with the fingertips and jab it into the foe's *. Done right, the foe can't speak or move and just stands frozen. If an amateur tries, or hesitates, the user risks injury. The name Three-Year Death comes from a rumor that in a tournament for this move, many losers died three years later.
note: '*' kept as in source (censored target). Three-Year Death (glossary). Compressed to fit 312.

en: A stomp with a big, heavy bottom is harder to dodge than a normal foot stomp and does more damage. Partly it's just that the area is bigger than a foot, but more than that, anyone caught in this situation will freeze for an instant.

Once it clamps down, it is said to hold on with great force until its catch is split in two. If an ally gets caught, cast a fire spell at once. A clam roasted by fire soon opens its shell. Then rescue your ally right away.

A great fan also called the "Banana Leaf Fan". Tengu are said to raise winds and storms with it. Legend also says whoever holds a Tengu Fan gains the power to fly. That legend even suggests tengu may be humans who got hold of a Tengu Fan.
note: [JP] = Banana Leaf Fan; item name [JP] assumed 'Tengu Fan'.

en: If pitch-black clouds gather in the daytime sky, beware. The black lightning they unleash puts common lightning to shame. Struck by it, body and soul are burned away and held captive in the demon world, they say. To defend, get precious metals off your body at once.
note: [JP] kept generic 'black lightning' (item name not yet fixed).

en: The mightiest swallow-whole, warping space to gulp down even things too big to swallow. Once targeted, there is next to no escape.

Gloves made of tough animal hide. The outside is very hard leather, made for knocking foes down. But the inside is shock-absorbing material that protects your own fist. Truly gloves made for the fist.

Wasabi is a spice from the East, but it stings the nose more than the tongue, and differs a bit from what we eat daily. The sting can apparently be eased by breathing in through the nose. As for what role wasabi plays as a war banner, that's a long story, so let's save it for another time.
note: [JP] = war banner.

en: A war banner inscribed with the teaching "Strike the foe swift as lightning." The larger an army grows, the less mobile it becomes. The Hatamoto, a unit's leader so to speak, must deal properly with such problems too.
note: Hatamoto (chap slice_016).

en: A superhuman knee strike unleashed with genius flair. Its reach is long: at any opening, the user dashes in, steps up on the foe's body and delivers a humiliating knee. Truly a flash of a move, but it takes either the ultimate body or levitation magic adapted for speed.
note: [JP] = 'Shining Wizard' wrestling move; name not used in text.

en: The horn of a unicorn, ruler of purity. Hard to obtain, but it glows faintly even in darkness and is so beautiful it is highly prized as an antique. Since it is only the horn, anyone can touch it.

The horn of a bicorn, ruler of impurity. Bicorns are thought to be foes of unicorns, but some say a unicorn is a young bicorn that grows horns as it matures: the unicorn gave up understanding for purity, the bicorn knew the world at the cost of impurity. But is it true?
note: Compressed to fit 312.

en: A long, thick nail. From the far East, a charm came with it: on a night so dark even the moon hides, write the name of one you wish health and happiness, tie that person's hair to a Magic Puppet, and nail it to a tree with this nail.
note: Ironic 'health and happiness' kept as in source (it is a curse ritual). [JP] = magic puppet (glossary). [accuracy] Lead decision: magic puppet term = "Magic Puppet".

en: Pour boiling water in through the spout on top, and Atonewolo's Hot Jug shows its true worth. If you have one, set it on wrinkled clothes and move it as if smoothing them out. The wrinkles will vanish and the clothes will look as good as new.
note: New name Atnewolo ([JP]), romanization guessed; item name assumed 'Atnewolo's Hot Flask' (a clothes iron). [accuracy] Item name as in ITEM.CSV (review_g4): Atonewolo's Hot Jug.

en: Once the host is gone, the monsters in the Hivanask all start using their powers to protect themselves from enemies. That combined power may or may not easily surpass even their host, Seot Mar. Either way, it is unwise to wake a sleeping child.
note: New names Hivanask ([JP]), Seot Mar ([JP]; Seot per glossary 'Seot's Demon Nest').

en: A whip for drilling manners into children of good families. Unlike a normal whip, it is shaped like a springy rod. A snappy blow is a real menace to a child, and can scar them for life. But if the wielder is attractive or worthy of respect, that strictness can be felt as love, they say.

You hear a knock, fling the door wide open, and no one is there. Thinking it odd, you close it, and a groan comes from outside. The one who opened it says it's the fault of whoever stood there. That makes some sense, yet it somehow feels unfair.
Being told "Come again!" feels nice, however roughly you're thrown out. You resolve not to get kicked out next time, but next time, too, you get kicked out with a "Come again!"

A leotard steeped in the pleasure of destruction. The snug fabric clings to the skin with a suction-like fit, so much so that you could think you were wearing nothing. That strange feeling brings an even greater thrill.

A mysterious barrier the Ryug possess. The Ryug alter it to suit their own nature as they go into battle. It takes three broad forms, but it is said some Aura Steeda change into something that fits none of the three.
note: Ryug (glossary). New name Aura Steeda ([JP]), romanization guessed.

en: In full, the Camp Edict on Regular Tuna. A helmet made by the Eastern lords called Daimyo. It was the first law on tuna, revered as divine in Eastern culture. Warriors and the court once feuded over tuna, but this helmet's enactment made tuna part of the cuisine, and peace came. --Eastern Records
note: [JP]: [JP] read as tuna grade ('regular'). New terms Daimyo, Eastern Records ([JP]).

en: The helmet worn by Taizarti, Demon Duke of the direct line. It is a plain iron helmet, but the Kin of Darkness know whose it is, and all who see it tremble in fear. With this helmet, it is said, the Sea of the Wastes is as good as conquered.
note: Taizarti (glossary), [JP] = Demon Duke (chap slice_019). New: Sea of the Wastes ([JP]). Item name not used.

en: A white cloth often worn by ghosts born in Eastern lands. It is said to mark a ghost's rank, so aiming at the cloth may rattle them. Snatch it and run, and you can enjoy a game of tag to the ends of the earth, with your life on the line.
note: [JP] (hitai-eboshi); name not used in text.

en: The noble armor of a royal palace knight. Its beautiful ornaments nurture the wearer's heart and instill dignity worthy of the armor. The more you wear it, the better you will know the importance of the duty called Imperial Guard.
Armor said to hold the magic of obsidian. Wear it, and it will guard you like a solid tortoise-shell wall.
note: Four Symbols set (tortoise/phoenix/tiger/dragon) with 2345-2347.

en: The trousers worn by Don Magus. They look hard to move in, but try them on and you'll be amazed how easy they are. The cloth carries a light magic that lets the sluggish move fairly well. It is thanks to Big Daddy that Don Magus moves in ways that don't fit that build.
note: New name Don Magus ([JP]); gender not stated, no pronouns.

en: A sword Undine holds dear. Only a knight she has opened her heart to may wield it. The water clan cherishes Undine; should anyone make her cry, the whole clan will come for revenge. Do you have the heart to answer her devotion?
note: Undine ([JP] in source).

en: In Eastern culture, the hadajuban is apparently seen as underwear. It is also common garb for the dead, so it seems essential for Eastern ghosts. When wet, the cloth turns see-through. A young maiden bathing in a hadajuban would make a picture all on her own.
A corset laced so tight its tip has become pointed. Wear this, and you too can gain a wonderfully toned body! ...Maybe. Rumor has it the tip of this corset actually leads to the "Point".
note: [JP] unclear reference; rendered literally as "Point".

en: Gauntlets said to hold the magic of ruby. Worn on both arms, their trail of rubies seems to blaze like a phoenix.
Shoes the pale color of ivory. Wear them, and a noble heart dwells in you, giving you the strength and beauty of a tiger, they say.
A mantle that gives off a deep blue light. Wear it, and as an incarnation of the blue water dragon, you are said to gain rare wisdom.
A fashion item made for people without facial hair. Put it on and any face turns pretty, so pretty that no one can resist teasing you.

"Furugatari Mutsusumeragi Norito." It uses the character for land, so you might think it a prayer to the earth, but apparently not. What could "Land King" mean? This prayer is a blood scroll, written in blood. Whose blood, no one knows.
note: Reading of [JP] given in source; romanized. [accuracy] Matches the item name Old Land-King Prayer (review_g4).
